entry_id.description: Optional. Without it, all pool pumps are affected.

num_repeats.name: Repeats
num_repeats.description: Optional. Without it the setting of the remote applies.

entity_missing.title: Entity missing: {entity}
entity_missing.description: The function "{entry}" ({function}) uses the entity {entity}, which no longer exists (deleted or renamed). Select an existing entity in the settings of the function or restore the entity. This notice disappears by itself as soon as it exists again or is no longer used.

device_missing.title: Push target missing: {entity}
device_missing.description: The function "{entry}" ({function}) sends push notifications to a device ({entity}) that no longer exists (e.g. the companion app was removed). Select an existing device in the settings. This notice disappears by itself as soon as the target is valid again.

legacy_entry.title: Old format: {entry}
legacy_entry.description: The entry "{entry}" comes from an older version (one instance or one function per entry) and is no longer loaded. Delete it, then create the “Functions” hub and add the instances with the “Add …” buttons.

llm_auth_failed.title: Access denied: {entry}
llm_auth_failed.description: The provider rejected the key of the function "{entry}" (LLM usage): invalid, revoked, expired or not an admin key (a normal API key is not enough). Anthropic: Console → Settings → Admin keys; OpenAI: organization settings → Admin keys. Enter a valid admin key in the settings of the function. This notice disappears by itself as soon as the query works again.

general.name: General
general.description: Sensor (vibration sensor or the two door contacts), lockout time and automatic reset.

data_description.vibration_sensor: Alternative to the two door contacts: binary sensor that triggers when mail is dropped in. Use either this or the contacts, not both.
data_description.debounce_seconds: Further triggers within this time are ignored; the removal door is also ignored this long after a delivery.
data_description.name: Optional. Empty = “Mailbox notification”. Enter only the name of the instance, e.g. “Office”; the function name is prepended automatically.
data_description.delivery_contact: Door contact of the delivery flap; opening it counts as mail dropped in. Requires the removal contact, not combined with the vibration sensor.
data_description.empty_contact: Door contact of the removal door; opening it marks the mailbox as emptied (only if mail is recorded).

notifications.name: Notifications
notifications.description: How and with what text you are told about mail.

data.mobile_action: Show "Mailbox emptied" action in the push notification

data_description.mobile_action: Adds a button (iOS and Android) to the notification that marks the mailbox as emptied.
data_description.repeat_message: Sent when the sensor triggers again while mail is still present (with the "emptied" action).
data_description.mobile_targets: Devices with the Home Assistant companion app. Multiple devices possible; sent via the notify.mobile_app_… service of the device.

new_door_guard.title: Door guard
new_door_guard.description: All settings of the door on one page. Empty fields are off; only “Door” is expanded.

door.name: Door
door.description: Lock, door contact and the sensors needed for automatic unlocking and locking.

data_description.name: Optional. Empty = “Door guard”. Enter only the name of the instance, e.g. “Office”; the function name is prepended automatically.
data_description.contact: Reports the door open (on) or closed (off). Required for the warning and for the check before locking.
data_description.presence_entities: People or device trackers that count as present, e.g. the parents. Do not add children. Needed for presence triggers and conditions.
data_description.workday_sensor: Binary sensor that is on on work or school days (e.g. a workday sensor). Needed for a different time on days off.

unlock.name: Unlocking
unlock.description: Automatic unlocking. Empty fields are off.

data.unlock_only_when_home: Only unlock at those times if someone is home

data_description.unlock_time_workday: Applies when the workday sensor is on. Without a sensor it applies every day.
data_description.unlock_time_free: Applies when the workday sensor is off. Needs the workday sensor.
data_description.unlock_on_arrival: Needs the people for presence. Nothing is made up for if someone is already home.
data_description.unlock_only_if_on: All selected entities must be on. People and trackers count as on when home. If a state is unclear, nothing is unlocked.
data_description.unlock_skip_if_on: If one of the entities is on (e.g. vacation), nothing is unlocked.

lock.name: Locking
lock.description: Automatic locking. Empty fields and unchecked boxes are off.

data.lock_closed_seconds: Lock when the door has been closed for (seconds, 0 = off)

data_description.lock_when_away: Needs the people for presence. If someone returns during the wait, it is cancelled.
data_description.lock_only_if_on: All selected entities must be on. If a state is unclear, it still locks.
data_description.lock_skip_if_on: If one of the entities is on, nothing is locked.

window_edit.description: The pump is switched on at the start and off at the end. If the end is earlier than the start, the window runs past midnight. The days refer to the day the window starts.

dry_run.title: Dry-run detection
dry_run.description: Detects a pump running dry: the pump is on and the power stays between the lower and upper limit for the set duration. Without a power sensor the feature is off. An alarm stays until acknowledged or the pump is restarted.

heater.description: Switches the heater by temperature: on at the switch-on threshold (or above), off at the switch-off threshold (or below); in between it stays as it is. Without a heater the function is off. The pump is not taken into account.

data_description.heater_entity: Leave empty to not control a heater.
data_description.heater_off_below: Must be below the switch-on threshold (hysteresis).

new_llm_usage.title: LLM usage
new_llm_usage.description:
Monitors the costs and remaining balance of an LLM API account (Anthropic or OpenAI). This needs an **admin key** of the organization; a normal API key does not work.

**Anthropic:** Claude Console → Settings → Admin keys → Create key (organization admins only; a personal account without an organization does not have it, set up an organization under Settings → Organization first).

**OpenAI:** platform.openai.com → organization settings → Admin keys → Create new admin key (organization owners only) and select the permission for usage and costs.

The admin key can also manage members and keys, so keep it safe. Like all credentials it is stored unencrypted in Home Assistant's storage. The providers only report costs per day; the remaining balance is calculated from them (UTC days, reports delayed by a few hours).

data_description.name: Optional. Empty = “LLM usage”. Enter only the name of the instance, e.g. “Anthropic”; the function name is prepended automatically.
data_description.api_key: Admin key of the organization (Anthropic: sk-ant-admin01-…, OpenAI: admin key with the permission for usage and costs). It is only used to query the costs.
data_description.mode: “Balance”: you enter the current balance from the console (and again after every top-up via “Calibrate balance”); the remaining balance is the amount minus the costs since then. “Monthly budget”: the remaining budget is the amount minus the costs of the current month. With automatic top-up choose “Monthly budget”, otherwise the remaining balance is wrong.
data_description.amount: Balance mode: your current balance according to the provider's console. Monthly budget: the amount you want to spend per month. In the provider's currency (currently USD).
data_description.poll_minutes: How often the costs are queried. The providers' reports are delayed by a few hours.
data_description.track_usage: In addition to the costs, query tokens (and requests for OpenAI) for today and the month. Needs one more query per interval.

limits.name: Limits
limits.description: When warnings are sent. Empty fields do not warn.

data.low_balance: Warn when the balance falls below …
data.forecast_warning: Warn when the forecast exceeds the limit

data_description.low_balance: Empty = no warning. Applies to the remaining balance or budget; pointless with automatic top-up.
data_description.daily_limit: Empty = no warning. Warns once a day when the cost of the day (UTC) exceeds the limit.
data_description.monthly_limit: Empty = no warning. Warns once a month when the cost of the month (UTC) exceeds the limit.
data_description.forecast_warning: Warns once a month when the forecast of the monthly cost exceeds the monthly limit (or the budget in monthly budget mode) before it is actually exceeded.

notifications.description: How and with what warnings are sent.

new_energy_monitor.title: Energy monitor
new_energy_monitor.description: Splits grid import and PV self-consumption between two units in proportion to their simultaneous use and calculates the settlement. It is a calculation aid, not tax or legal advice. Counting starts when it is set up.

meters.name: Meters
meters.description: Energy sensors in kWh that keep counting up. The sub-meters must measure the consumption including PV power (the inverter feeds in before them).

data_description.name: Optional. Empty = “Energy monitor”.
data_description.meter_a_energy: Unit A pays the energy costs centrally.
data_description.meter_b_energy: Unit B operates the PV system and reimburses its share.

units.name: Units
units.description: Names of the two dwellings and the keys for water and gas: water is split by persons, gas by living area (or persons).

prices.name: Prices
prices.description: Basis of the settlement. All prices gross, as shown on the invoice.

data.pv_price: Price per PV kWh used by unit A (ct/kWh)
data.base_fee_share_b: Share of unit B in the base fee (%)

data_description.grid_price: Total price per kWh of grid import, for example 34.
data_description.pv_price: What unit A is charged for the PV power it uses. Pick one or type your own value. The self-consumption tariff stays with the system operator.
data_description.base_fee_monthly: Split by the share; 0 = no base fee.
data_description.base_fee_share_b: The rest goes to unit A.

water.name: Water (optional)
water.description: One shared water meter for both units. The cost is split by the number of persons (showering, washing, cooking).

data_description.water_meter: Sensor in m³ that keeps counting up. Empty = no water settlement.
data_description.water_price: Total price per m³ incl. waste water.

gas.name: Gas (optional)
gas.description: One shared gas meter for both units. Heating dominates, so the default key is living area.

data_description.gas_meter: Sensor in m³ that keeps counting up. Empty = no gas settlement.
data_description.gas_price: Price per m³ as invoiced (use the price per m³, not per kWh).

common.name: Common electricity (optional)
common.description: Gas boiler, outdoor lighting, router and similar run through unit A's sub-meter. This part is moved to unit B according to the key before grid import and PV are split. Without a meter, enter a constant power; with a meter the power is ignored. Empty and 0 = no correction.

data_description.common_meter: Optional energy sensor (kWh, counting up) of these consumers, e.g. a plug with measurement on the boiler and router. It must be part of unit A's consumption.
data_description.common_power: Average power of the common consumers, counted per elapsed time. It is limited by the consumption of unit A.
data_description.common_key: Living area (default), persons or half each.

em_settings.title: Energy monitor
em_settings.description: Splits grid import and PV self-consumption between two units in proportion to their simultaneous use and calculates the settlement. It is a calculation aid, not tax or legal advice. Counting starts when it is set up.

meters.name: Meters
meters.description: Energy sensors in kWh that keep counting up. The sub-meters must measure the consumption including PV power (the inverter feeds in before them).

data_description.name: Optional. Empty = “Energy monitor”.
data_description.meter_a_energy: Unit A pays the energy costs centrally.
data_description.meter_b_energy: Unit B operates the PV system and reimburses its share.

units.name: Units
units.description: Names of the two dwellings and the keys for water and gas: water is split by persons, gas by living area (or persons).

prices.name: Prices
prices.description: Basis of the settlement. All prices gross, as shown on the invoice.

data.pv_price: Price per PV kWh used by unit A (ct/kWh)
data.base_fee_share_b: Share of unit B in the base fee (%)

data_description.grid_price: Total price per kWh of grid import, for example 34.
data_description.pv_price: What unit A is charged for the PV power it uses. Pick one or type your own value. The self-consumption tariff stays with the system operator.
data_description.base_fee_monthly: Split by the share; 0 = no base fee.
data_description.base_fee_share_b: The rest goes to unit A.

water.name: Water (optional)
water.description: One shared water meter for both units. The cost is split by the number of persons (showering, washing, cooking).

data_description.water_meter: Sensor in m³ that keeps counting up. Empty = no water settlement.
data_description.water_price: Total price per m³ incl. waste water.

gas.name: Gas (optional)
gas.description: One shared gas meter for both units. Heating dominates, so the default key is living area.

data_description.gas_meter: Sensor in m³ that keeps counting up. Empty = no gas settlement.
data_description.gas_price: Price per m³ as invoiced (use the price per m³, not per kWh).

common.name: Common electricity (optional)
common.description: Gas boiler, outdoor lighting, router and similar run through unit A's sub-meter. This part is moved to unit B according to the key before grid import and PV are split. Without a meter, enter a constant power; with a meter the power is ignored. Empty and 0 = no correction.

data_description.common_meter: Optional energy sensor (kWh, counting up) of these consumers, e.g. a plug with measurement on the boiler and router. It must be part of unit A's consumption.
data_description.common_power: Average power of the common consumers, counted per elapsed time. It is limited by the consumption of unit A.
data_description.common_key: Living area (default), persons or half each.

error.duplicate_meter: Each meter may only be chosen once.
error.invalid_price: The price per PV kWh must be a number from 0 up, for example 16.26.
error.no_persons: Enter the number of persons for at least one unit.
error.no_area: Enter the living area for at least one unit.

new_energy_cost.title: Energy cost
new_energy_cost.description: Counts the energy and cost of an existing device, for example a plug that measures power. Counting starts when it is set up.

source.name: Device
source.description: The sensor that measures the device’s consumption.

data_description.name: Optional. Empty = “Energy cost”. Best use the device name, e.g. “Freezer”.
data_description.source_entity: A sensor in W or kW (power) or in Wh, kWh or MWh (energy meter). The kind is recognised by the unit. Leave empty for a device without measurement (see below).

fixed.name: Device without measurement
fixed.description: Instead of a measuring sensor: while the entity is on, the fixed power is counted. Either a measuring sensor or an entity, not both.

data.fixed_entity: Entity (shows whether the device is running)

data_description.fixed_entity: e.g. a light, a switch, a binary sensor, a media player or an air conditioner. Off means off, idle, standby and paused, everything else counts as on.
data_description.fixed_power: The power of the device in operation, e.g. from the data sheet.
data_description.scale_brightness: The power is then calculated from the light’s brightness (0 to 255) between 0 and the configured power.

price.name: Price
price.description: What the consumption is valued at. A price entity (e.g. a dynamic tariff) replaces the fixed price; if it fails, the last valid price applies first, otherwise the fixed one.

data_description.price_ct: Total price per kWh, e.g. 34. Required without a price entity.
data_description.price_entity: Sensor, input_number or number with the current price per kWh.
data_description.price_unit: €/kWh or ct/kWh, depending on what the price entity provides.

history.name: Existing values (optional)
history.description: So the totals do not start at zero: either backfilled from the long-term statistics or with your own start values, or both.

data_description.history_from: Calculates energy and cost from this day on from the sensor’s hourly statistics up to the start of counting (only with a measuring sensor that has a state class). Prices come from the price entity’s statistics, otherwise the fixed or current price applies. Runs once per date; a new date replaces the backfill.
data_description.start_kwh: Added to the energy total (day, month and year stay unchanged).
data_description.start_cost: Added to the cost total (day, month and year stay unchanged).

error.unsupported_unit: The sensor must measure power (W, kW) or energy (Wh, kWh, MWh).
error.source_or_fixed: Choose either a measuring sensor or an entity with a fixed power, not both and not neither.
error.no_power: Enter the power of the device in W.
